failures.criterion: Approved spec version 11, 'What Envoy copies': 'One rule, for every Slack message: the delivered text is the message's own text, then every piece of display text it carries in its attachments and blocks' — and 'It never has to know the kind of a block or an attachment' and 'There is no list of message kinds, and the one exception is a deleted message'.
failures.evidence: Round 2 adds a second exception keyed on a block kind name: `slackDeliveredText` sets `skipRichText` when the message's own text holds a non-whitespace character, and `walk` then returns from any object whose `type` is `rich_text`, at any depth (packages/envoy/internal/contracts/normalize.go:1118, 1180-1182). The ruling's stated reason — that the tree is the Slack client's structured copy of the message's own words — does not hold for an app that posts a rich_text block of its own content, and for such a message the words are now dropped entirely. Driven on a real nats-server, a real envoy-listener built from this head and a subscribed session, posted to over /webhook/slack (`CASES=packages/envoy/out/e2e/infra180-rt-cases.jsonl bash packages/envoy/out/e2e/infra180-tester-rig.sh`): a `bot_message` with `text` `"Build failed"` and one `rich_text` block carrying `"FAIL TestFoo at line 42: want 3, got 4"` delivered `text=Build failed`; the same with a `section` block beside the `rich_text` one delivered `text=Build failed\npipeline 991`, the rich_text words gone; and the same `rich_text` block nested inside an attachment delivered `text=Build failed`. This is the issue's own symptom — the words the message carries do not reach the agent — reintroduced for one block kind, and it is the shape Slack tells app authors to post: 'you must either: include all necessary content for screen reader users in the top-level `text` field of your message, or do not include a top-level `text` field if the message has `blocks`' (docs.slack.dev/block-kit, 'Accessibility considerations'), and 'Use rich text for formatted output. When displaying agent-generated content, prefer rich text blocks over markdown' (same page, 'Block Kit and AI', best practice 1). Red test: `an app's rich-text words beside a short text of its own` in packages/envoy/internal/contracts/normalize_test.go, committed at 0a049686. `cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/contracts/ -count=1 -run "TestSlackDeliveredText/an_app's_rich-text_words_beside_a_short_text_of_its_own"` fails at this head with `payload["text"] = "Build failed" (present true), want "Build failed\nFAIL TestFoo at line 42: want 3, got 4" (present true)`. Narrowing that keeps every case the architect weighed: skip a rich_text object only when every display string it carries is already held by the message's own text once Slack's three entities are resolved — the client's copy satisfies that by construction and an app's own content does not — or whatever narrowing the architect prefers. Either way the fix is the architect's design call, not the red test's.
